issues.legal_issue: A writ challenge to a land acquisition may be dismissed for delay and laches when it is brought after possession has been taken and the award has become final, particularly where the delay is unexplained.
material_facts: The landowners objected to the acquisition and initially challenged it in a court that lacked territorial jurisdiction; that challenge ended when the Supreme Court set aside the interim order for want of jurisdiction.
After that proceeding ended, the landowners did not challenge the acquisition for a period and gave no explanation for the delay; a later writ petition was withdrawn and then refiled.
The Supreme Court treated possession as having been taken and the award as having become final before the writ challenge was determined.
The landowners also sought enhancement of compensation through a reference proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The writ petition and appeal were dismissed for delay and laches, without deciding the merits of the acquisition; the High Court's dismissal was affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: The discretionary power under Article 226 should not ordinarily be exercised to quash acquisition proceedings where there is inordinate, unexplained delay and the acquisition has progressed to possession and a final award. The Court relied on Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay v. Industrial Development Investment Co. Pvt. Ltd. (1996) 11 SCC 501, State of Rajasthan v. D.R. Laxmi (1996) 6 SCC 445, Municipal Council, Ahmednagar v. Shah Hyder Beig (2000) 2 SCC 48, and C. Padma v. Deputy Secretary to the Government of Tamil Nadu (1997) 2 SCC 627. It also referred to the vesting consequence described in Section 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

rule.if: writ_challenge_to_land_acquisition and unexplained_delay and possession_preceded_writ and award_was_final

predicates.writ_challenge_to_land_acquisition: The landowner brought a writ proceeding challenging the land acquisition.
predicates.unexplained_delay: The landowner left a period without pursuing the acquisition challenge and gave no explanation for that delay.
predicates.possession_preceded_writ: The acquiring authority had taken possession of the acquired land before the writ challenge was brought.
predicates.award_was_final: The award for the acquired land had become final.

issues.definition: When a landowner brings a writ challenge to a land acquisition after unexplained delay, after possession has been taken and after the award is final, the challenge is dismissed for delay and laches.
